info.title: VpnHood! MANAGER
info.description:
The REST API of VpnHood! MANAGER, the panel that runs VPN servers and gives out the access keys people connect with.
The panel is built on this API, so a script or a service can do anything it does: give access keys to your customers,
add and install servers, and read their usage. Every path is under `https://api.vpnhood.com`.

The guide [Call the MANAGER API](https://developer.vpnhood.com/manager-api/) goes from a key to a first request.

## Sign in with a bot's API key

A script signs in as a bot: a member of your project's team, with a role and an API key.

1. In the panel, open **Settings**, select **Team**, then **Add Bot**, and name the bot.
2. The panel shows the bot's key once, as the value of an `Authorization` header. Copy it.
3. The bot joins as `ProjectReader`, which only reads. Open its page and give it the role its work needs:
   `AccessTokenWriter` to give out access keys, `ProjectWriter` to manage servers too.

Send the key with every request:

```http
Authorization: Bearer <the bot's key>
```

Each operation says which permission it needs and which roles have it. A request without a valid key gets `401`, and
one whose role lacks the permission gets `403`. If a key leaks, reset it on the bot's page: the old one stops working
at once.

## Ids, lists and changes

- `projectId` is the id in your project's address in the panel:
  `https://console.vpnhood.com/projects/{projectId}/overview`. The other ids are the ones the API returns.
- A list takes `recordIndex`, the first item to return, and `recordCount`, how many to return.
- An update (`PATCH`) takes only the fields to change, each as `{ "value": ... }`. A field left out keeps its value.
- Times are in UTC, in ISO 8601.

## Errors

An error has a status code and a JSON body, whose `TypeName` names the error and `Message` says what went wrong:

```json
{ "TypeName": "NotExistsException", "Message": "..." }
```

`404` means not found, `409` already exists, and `400` any other request the API refuses.

get.summary: Get the key to paste into the app
get.description:
The access key itself, as a JSON string that starts with `vh:`: it carries the servers of the key's server
farm, the key's name, tags and support code, and its profile's client policies. It fails with 400 while that
farm has no server to put in it.

**Access:** the `AccessTokenReadAccessKey` permission, which `AccessTokenWriter`, `ProjectWriter`, `ProjectAdmin` and `ProjectOwner` have.

The keys the list gives for the same filters, a row each: support code, name, premium code, management code, id,
server farm, group, profile and, with `includeAccessKey`, the access key. It holds 51 keys unless
`recordCount` says more. The codes are empty, and `includeAccessKey` is refused, unless the caller may
read access keys (`AccessTokenReadAccessKey`).

**Access:** the `ProjectRead` permission, which `ProjectReader`, `AccessTokenWriter`, `ProjectWriter`, `ProjectAdmin` and `ProjectOwner` have.

Makes a self-signed certificate for the farm; a wildcard domain is refused. One for a domain the farm already
has replaces that one, keeping its visibility if that was higher. With `AutoSign`, the MANAGER then asks
Let's Encrypt to sign it. The farm's servers take it within about a minute, unless it is `DomainOnly`. The
free plan holds up to 25 certificates; one more fails with `QuotaException`, unless it replaces one.

**Access:** the `CertificateWrite` permission, which `ProjectWriter`, `ProjectAdmin` and `ProjectOwner` have.

arrives, it joins the server's access points, the server's `autoConfigure` turns off, and
`oldIpAddress` is released; with no IP after a day, the order fails. Ordering again while the server's
order is pending returns that order, and an order the provider refuses fails the call and is kept as failed.

**Access:** the `ProjectWrite` permission, which `ProjectWriter`, `ProjectAdmin` and `ProjectOwner` have.

token.

`SyncCacheSize`. `UdpEndPoints` and `QuicEndPoints` take only `[]`, which turns UDP or QUIC
off. A setting the MANAGER doesn't know is dropped.

idleServerCount.description: The servers that work, with no session.

notInstalledServerCount.description: The servers that have not reached the MANAGER yet.

tunnelReceiveSpeed.description: The speed the active servers' tunnels receive at, together, in bytes per second.

usingBandwidth.description:
Meant as the bandwidth the active servers use, in bytes per second: it is four times `tunnelReceiveSpeed`,
as `tunnelSendSpeed` is left out.

ServerState.description:
A server's state, from its reports to the MANAGER.

- `NotInstalled`: It has not reached the MANAGER yet.
- `Disabled`: It reports, but `isEnabled` is off, so it gets no new sessions.
- `Lost`: It has sent no status for over three minutes, so it gets no new sessions.
- `Error`: It could not use its settings, so it gets no new sessions; `lastConfigError` says why.
- `Configuring`: It is taking new settings, which takes a minute or two; it still gets new sessions.
- `Idle`: It works, with no session.
- `Active`: It works, with sessions.

udpConnectionCount.description: The UDP connections it opens for its sessions.

availableMemory.description: The machine's available memory, in bytes; null where not known.

availableSwapMemoryMb.description: The machine's free swap, in megabytes; null where the server does not manage swap (it does on Linux).

cpuUsage.description: The machine's CPU use, in percent; null where not known.

tunnelSendSpeed.description: The speed its tunnels send at, in bytes per second.

tunnelReceiveSpeed.description: The speed its tunnels receive at, in bytes per second.

sessionCount.description: The most sessions the servers had open together in the step.

tunnelTransferSpeed.description: The servers' top tunnel speed together in the step, sent and received, in bytes per second.

cpuUsage.description: The server's top CPU use in the step, in percent; 0 unless `serverId` is given.

availableMemory.description: The server's least available memory in the step, in bytes; 0 unless `serverId` is given.

ServerStatusHistory.description: The servers' load in one step of a period; a step in which no server reported has zeros.

generateNewSecret.description:
`true` to give the server a new management secret, which its install commands carry from then on;
VpnHood! SERVER does not use it.

autoConfigure.description: Whether the MANAGER is to set the server's access points by itself.

accessPoints.description:
The server's new access points, up to 10. They turn `autoConfigure` off, unless the same request sets it
on: then the MANAGER rebuilds them from the server's own addresses, keeping their ports.

allowInAutoLocation.description: Whether apps that leave their location on Auto may be sent to the server.

isEnabled.description: Whether the server is to take new sessions.

tags.description: The server's new tags, all of them; a missing `#` is added.

clientFilterId.description: The id of the server's new client filter, or null for none.

configSwapMemorySizeMb.description:
The swap the server is to have in all, in megabytes, from 10 to 100,000, or null for its server profile's
setting.

ServerUpdateParams.description: The fields of a server to change; one left out keeps its value.

SigningType.description:
How a certificate gets signed: the panel's Signing.

- `Manual`: The MANAGER leaves it as it is.
- `AutoSign`: The MANAGER has Let's Encrypt sign it, and renews it about 30 days before it expires. Let's Encrypt checks the
domain over plain HTTP on TCP port 80, so the domain must point at one of the farm's servers, with that port
open. A failed attempt is tried again about once a day; after 6 failures in a row it goes back to
`Manual`.
- `DomainOnly`: For a domain whose certificate lives elsewhere, such as a CDN's in front of the servers: the servers never get
it, and in the keys it gives apps the domain alone, on port 443.

SubscriptionType.description:
A project's plan.

- `Free`: The free plan: it caps how many server farms, servers, access keys, profiles, groups, certificates and client
filters a project has, and how long a period a usage report covers.
- `Unlimited`: The plan without those caps.

UploadMethod.description:
How the MANAGER uploads a farm's update file to an update URL: the panel's Auto Upload.

- `None`: It doesn't: you put the file there yourself, again after every change.
- `Post`: With an HTTP POST to the file URL.
- `Put`: With an HTTP PUT to the file URL.
- `PutPost`: With an HTTP PUT, then a POST if the PUT fails.

sentTraffic.description: The bytes the devices sent through the VPN in the period.

receivedTraffic.description: The bytes the devices received through the VPN in the period.

deviceCount.description: How many devices used the VPN in the period.

serverCount.description: Not counted: null, or 0 when there was no usage.

confirmedTime.description: When the caller first opened the project; null until then, as just after someone added them to its team.

that needs an ad; null for a caller who may not change the project.

serverFarmId.description: The id of the server farm it belongs to.

serverFarmName.description: The name of that server farm.

location.description:
Where the server is, found from its public IP address when it first took its settings; null until then, or when
that address could not be located.

version.description: The version of VpnHood! SERVER it runs; null until it first connects.

environmentVersion.description: The version of the .NET runtime it runs on; null until it first connects.

osInfo.description: The machine and its OS, as the server describes them; null until it first connects.

tcpCongestionControl.description:
The TCP congestion control the machine's OS runs, such as `bbr`; null where the server does not manage its
network (it does on Linux).

machineName.description: The machine's name; null until the server first connects.

totalMemory.description: The machine's memory, in bytes; null until the server first connects, and 0 where it could not tell.

totalSwapMemoryMb.description: The machine's swap in all, in megabytes; null where the server does not manage swap (it does on Linux).

logicalCoreCount.description: The machine's logical cores; null until the server first connects.

configureTime.description: When the server last took its settings from the MANAGER; null until it first connects.

autoConfigure.description:
Whether the MANAGER sets the server's access points by itself, from the addresses the server finds, and follows
them when they change.

isEnabled.description:
Whether the server takes new sessions: a disabled one gets none, and apps that reach it are sent to another
server of the farm.

description.description: A note on the server; nothing in the API sets it, so it is null.

lastConfigError.description: Why the server could not use its last settings: the error it reported, as JSON; null when it could.

serverStatus.description: The server's last status report; null while it is `NotInstalled` or `Lost`.

accessPoints.description: The server's addresses: those it listens on, and those that go to apps.

tags.description:
The server's tags, each a `#` and letters, digits, `_` or `:`, which apps see with its location.
`#premium` keeps the server for premium sessions, such as trials; `#unblockable` marks one meant to
work where VPNs are blocked, which the MANAGER chooses for new sessions only after the others.

clientFilterId.description: The id of the server's client filter, which decides which clients it serves; null for all clients.

clientFilterName.description: The name of that client filter; null when the server has none.

configSwapMemorySizeMb.description:
The swap the server is set to have in all, in megabytes, where it manages swap (Linux): its own swap file makes
up what the machine's other swap lacks. Null for its server profile's setting.

tags.name: Projects
tags.description:
A project holds everything else: its server farms and servers, its access keys and its team. Every other path
starts with the project's id.

tags.name: ServerFarms
tags.description:
A server farm is a group of servers that share access keys: a key works on every server of its farm. The farm also
holds the certificate its keys carry and the server profile its servers run with.

tags.name: Servers
tags.description:
A server is a machine that runs VpnHood! SERVER for one of the project's server farms. Add it here, install VpnHood!
SERVER on it over SSH or with its install command, and follow its state.

tags.name: ServerProfiles
tags.description:
A server profile holds the settings of servers. Each server farm uses one, and the MANAGER sends its settings to
every server of the farm, so they change in one place.

tags.name: Certificates
tags.description:
The SSL/TLS certificates of a server farm: its servers present them at the start of every connection, and its
access keys carry the domain of one. The MANAGER makes them, takes yours, or has Let's Encrypt sign one and renews
it.

tags.name: FarmTokenRepos
tags.description:
A server farm's update URLs, which the panel calls Farm Token URLs: files on the web where the MANAGER publishes the
farm's connection details, encrypted, so that apps that can't connect fetch them and find the farm's servers again.

tags.name: AccessTokens
tags.description:
Access keys are what users paste into the app to connect: each reaches the servers of one server farm and takes its
limits from an access key profile.

tags.name: AccessTokenProfiles
tags.description:
Access key profiles set what the access keys made from them allow: traffic, speed, devices, lifetime, ads, and the
plans offered in each country. A change reaches every key of the profile.

tags.name: AccessTokenGroups
tags.description:
Access key groups put access keys in named sets, to list, export and delete them together. A group changes nothing
in what its keys allow.

tags.name: Accesses
tags.description:
VPN users are the uses of access keys, each with its traffic: a public key has one for each device that connects
with it, and a private key one that all its devices share.

tags.name: Devices
tags.description:
Devices that have connected with the project's access keys, each known by the client id its app made for it. A
locked device can't connect.

tags.name: Report
tags.description:
The project's usage over a period: its traffic, its devices and their countries, and its servers' load.

A period that ends now may be answered with figures up to a thirtieth of its length old, a day at most. While the
report can't be read, a call fails with 503: try again later.

tags.name: ClientFilters
tags.description:
A client filter is a rule over a client's tags, and a server that has one serves only the clients it matches. Give
it to a server with the server's `clientFilterId`.

tags.name: IpLocks
tags.description:
Locked IPs: a device that connects from a locked IP address is refused, whichever of the project's access keys it
uses. An IP may also be listed without a lock, to keep a note on it.

tags.name: HostOrders
tags.description:
Host IPs are the IP addresses of the project's servers at their hosting provider, and host orders buy new ones.
They need a hosting provider set up for the project, which this API does not do: the project's
`hastHostProvider` tells whether it has one.

tags.name: Team
tags.description:
A project's team: the people and the bots who work on it, each with one role. Its `resourceId` is the project's
id. A bot is a member for a script, with an API key in place of a sign-in.

tags.name: PasswordAuthentication
tags.description:
The panel's accounts with an email and a password: create one, verify its email, reset its password, and sign in
with it. A script signs in with a bot's API key instead.

A refused call is a `PasswordAuthenticationException`, whose `Data.PasswordAuthenticationError` names the
reason: `InvalidCredential`, `EmailInUse`, `WeakPassword`, `InvalidEmail`,
`MissingPassword`, `UserDisabled`, `InvalidLink` or `TooManyRequests`. Calls are limited for
each IP address, for each email address and in all; over a limit, a call gets 429.

tags.name: System
tags.description: The service's own upkeep, to run by hand.

tags.name: Health
tags.description: A check that the service answers, for its own monitoring.
